## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Sattakkhattuparamakathā* (Kv 12.5) is a doctrinal controversy located in the twelfth chapter of the *Kathāvatthu*, the fifth book of the Theravāda Abhidhamma Piṭaka. The debate centers on the destiny of the *sattakkhattuparama*, the stream-enterer (*sotāpanna*) destined for a maximum of seven further rebirths [Dutt 1978]. According to Nalinaksha Dutt's analysis of the text and its tradition, the discourse counters a thesis maintained by the Uttarāpathakas that such individuals must realize Nibbāna strictly after their seventh rebirth and cannot do so either earlier or later [Dutt 1978]. The Theravāda position rejects this rigid determination, arguing that an adept may accelerate their progress toward the goal through greater exertion or potentially delay advancement through unwholesome actions [Dutt 1978].
